deep.reconstruction:
Setting: E, F are Hilbert spaces. L^1 denotes trace-class (nuclear) operators and L_0 compact operators. rho_i(w) are the singular values in decreasing order, and |w| = (w*w)^{1/2}. alpha_n(u) is the n-th Fredholm coefficient, det(1+zu) = sum_n alpha_n(u) z^n. Lambda^n u is the n-th exterior power, normalised so that alpha_n(u) = Tr Lambda^n u and ||Lambda^n u||_1 = alpha_n(|u|) = e_n(rho(u)), the elementary symmetric function of the singular values (from the previous page). Section heading of the chapter: '5. Puissances exterieures d'op. de Fredholm, inegalites diverses'.

(i) Proof of Prop. 2 (eq. (11)): ||Lambda^p u wedge Lambda^q v||_1 <= p!q!/(p+q)! ||Lambda^p u||_1 ||Lambda^q v||_1.
- Write Schmidt decompositions u = sum rho_i bbar_i (x) a_i and v = sum sigma_j dbar_j (x) c_j.
- Expanding gives (1/(p+q)!) sum over multi-indices of rho_{i1}...rho_{ip} sigma_{j1}...sigma_{jq} times the rank-one operator (b_{i1} ^...^ d_{jq})bar (x) (a_{i1} ^...^ c_{jq}).
- Terms with a repeated i or j vanish. Grouping the p!q! orderings of each pair of increasing index sets gives the factor p!q!/(p+q)!.
- Each rank-one term has trace norm <= 1, since a wedge of unit vectors has norm <= 1 (Hadamard).
- The resulting sum factors as (e_p(rho(u)))(e_q(sigma(v))).

(ii) Corollary 2, eq. (14): alpha_m(|u+v|) <= sum_{p=0}^m alpha_p(|u|) alpha_{m-p}(|v|).
- Use alpha_m(|u+v|) = ||Lambda^m(u+v)|| _1 and the binomial expansion Lambda^m(u+v) = sum_p C(m,p) Lambda^p u wedge Lambda^{m-p} v.
- Apply (11); the binomial coefficients cancel against p!(m-p)!/m!.
- This is the coefficientwise form of Corollary 1, eq. (12)/(13): det(1+r|u+v|) <= det(1+r|u|) det(1+r|v|) for r >= 0. In singular values: prod(1+r rho_i(u+v)) <= prod(1+r rho_i(u)) prod(1+r rho_i(v)).

(iii) Theorem 2, the truncated version for compact u, v. With sigma_n^m(w) = e_m(rho_1(w),...,rho_n(w)) (eq. (17)):
- (15): prod_{i<=n}(1+r rho_i(u+v)) <= prod_{i<=n}(1+r rho_i(u)) prod_{i<=n}(1+r rho_i(v)).
- (16), its coefficientwise refinement: sigma_n^m(u+v) <= sum_p sigma_n^p(u) sigma_n^{m-p}(v).
- The proof is on the next page. It uses a variational formula, Prop. 3 / (18): sigma_n^m(u) = sup |alpha_m(wu)| = sup alpha_m(|wu|) over contractions w of rank <= n. This is a Ky Fan-type maximum principle for elementary symmetric functions of the top n singular values. The theorem then follows from (14) applied to wu, wv.
- For m = 1, (16) is Ky Fan's inequality: the sum of the top n singular values of u+v is at most the sum of those of u plus the sum of those of v.

Purpose: a systematic theory of Fredholm determinants and coefficients for nuclear operators. These are estimates for det(1+zu) and its coefficients under addition, in the line of 'La theorie de Fredholm' and 'Produits tensoriels topologiques'.
errors:
The argument is essentially correct. Small gaps:
- The 'on peut supposer ... distincts' step should state that terms with repeated indices vanish.
- The bound on the trace norm of each rank-one term by 1 (Hadamard's inequality for wedges of unit vectors) is used silently.
- The normalisation of Lambda^p (with 1/p!) must be the one making alpha_p = Tr Lambda^p u and ||Lambda^p u||_1 = e_p(rho); otherwise the constants p!q!/(p+q)! and the binomial cancellation are off.
In (15) the upper index of the products should be n (the truncation), not m, to be consistent with (16)-(17); either the handwriting or the transcription conflates m and n.
The final line is garbled. The special case that makes sense is m = 1 (Ky Fan's additive inequality for partial sums of singular values), not 'p = 1'.

ideas.what: Norm inequality ||Lambda^p u wedge Lambda^q v||_1 <= p!q!/(p+q)! ||Lambda^p u||_1 ||Lambda^q v||_1 via Schmidt decompositions
ideas.modern_name: trace-norm estimates for antisymmetric tensor products (multilinear-algebra technique of Bhatia's Matrix Analysis)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore / antisymmetric tensor technique (Weyl, Horn, Ky Fan era; systematized later by Bhatia and others)
ideas.where_published: possibly in the spirit of 'La theorie de Fredholm' (Bull. SMF 1956) or Produits tensoriels Ch. II; unsure

ideas.what: det(1+r|u+v|) <= det(1+r|u|) det(1+r|v|) for trace-class u, v
ideas.usually_credited_to: Rotfel'd (late 1960s, concave-function trace inequalities); Seiler-Simon (1975); Thompson's triangle inequality (1976)

ideas.what: Coefficientwise strengthening: e_m(s(u+v)) <= sum_p e_p(s(u)) e_{m-p}(s(v))
ideas.modern_name: elementary-symmetric (coefficientwise) refinement of the Seiler-Simon inequality
ideas.usually_credited_to: unclear; follows from Thompson's |A+B| <= U|A|U* + V|B|V* plus superadditivity facts; not commonly stated

ideas.what: Truncated version for compact operators with sigma_n^m = e_m of the top n singular values, proved through the variational formula sigma_n^m(u) = sup over rank-n contractions w of |alpha_m(wu)|
ideas.modern_name: Ky Fan maximum principle generalized to elementary symmetric functions; Rotfel'd/Thompson partial-sum inequalities
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ky Fan (1951) for m=1; Rotfel'd (1967-69) and Thompson (1976-77) for concave-function / partial versions

missed.claim: In 1953 Grothendieck proved det(1+r|u+v|) <= det(1+r|u|) det(1+r|v|) for nuclear operators on Hilbert space. He also proved its coefficientwise and top-n truncated refinements, which give Ky Fan's inequality as the case m=1. These predate Rotfel'd (late 1960s), Seiler-Simon (1975) and Thompson (1976), to whom the determinant inequality is usually credited.
missed.quote: (12) det(1+r|u+v|) <= det(1+r|u|)(det(1+r|v|)) ... (14) alpha_m(|u+v|) <= sum_{0<=p<=m} alpha_p(|u|) alpha_{m-p}(|v|) ... (16) sigma_n^m(u+v) <= sum_{p=0}^m sigma_n^p(u) sigma_n^{m-p}(v)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a priority/credit point for a standard trace-ideal inequality used in Fredholm determinant theory (Simon's Trace Ideals). The coefficientwise version, with its clean exterior-algebra proof, is rarely stated explicitly. The rank-n variational characterization of e_m(top-n singular values) is a tidy generalisation of Ky Fan's maximum principle.

deep.surprise_reason: The results are correct and the proofs are neat. They anticipate by 15-20 years a determinant inequality usually credited to Rotfel'd and Seiler-Simon, and give a coefficientwise, truncated form. Matrix analysts would not find the mathematics shocking: it follows from later general tools such as Thompson's triangle inequality and antisymmetric tensor techniques. Whether Grothendieck printed any of this in 'La theorie de Fredholm' or Produits tensoriels is uncertain, so the priority claim is only moderately strong.
transcription_corrections: 'On peut supposer [?] ... les (i_k) [?] ... distincts' is likely 'on peut se borner aux termes ou les (i_k) et les (j_l) sont deux a deux distincts' (terms with repetitions vanish).
In (15) the products should run over i = 1..n (truncation index), not 1..m.
The last line probably reads 'Comme cas particulier on trouve, pour m = 1, ... (inegalite de Ky Fan)', not 'pour p = 1'.
'L_0(E,F)' here likely denotes compact operators, as opposed to L^1, the nuclear/trace-class operators.
The margin note 'inutile a verifier' is uncertain; it may read 'inutile, a reecrire' or similar.
